verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same code fix: a Map from normalized email to its first index, with new arrivals registered in the map. Both preserve the first-match and within-upload duplicate behavior of findIndex. A also adds a regression test for the duplicate-existing-email edge case, the subtle behavior the Map rewrite could most easily break. B instead relies on a one-off equivalence check that was never committed. B's report has the stronger verification claim (identical output on a subset), but the lasting test protection tips it toward A.
a_issues: Did not compare old and new output field by field on the benchmark data, only the contact counts, as its report itself says.
b_issues: Adds no test for the first-entry-wins case when the stored book already has duplicate emails, which is the main behavior the Map rewrite must preserve.
The equivalence check against the old implementation was not kept in the repo, so it gives no ongoing protection.

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same fix to `src/import.ts`: a Map from normalized email to index, built once with first-entry-wins semantics, and updated as new contacts are appended. B also adds a regression test for the one subtle behavior the Map has to preserve: an incoming contact merges into the first of several existing entries with the same email. A's equivalence check against the old implementation is good evidence, but it was a one-off run and is not kept in the repo.
a_issues: No test added for first-entry-wins when the stored book already has duplicate emails, though this is the main behavior the Map has to preserve.
b_issues: Did not compare the old and new outputs field by field; the report says so openly.
